proof_summary: A binomial reindexing gives \(2nS_n=F_{2n+1}+F_{2n-1}-1\), so integrality would force \(2n\) to divide the right-hand side; Fibonacci periodicity modulo \(4,3,5\) rules this out when \(n\) has one of those small prime factors. Otherwise, for the least prime \(p\mid n\), roots of \(X^2-X-1\) over a splitting field of \(\mathbb F_p\) turn the assumed divisibility into an order dividing both \(12n\) and \(p^2-1\); minimality of \(p\) reduces this order to a divisor of \(12\), while a polynomial Bézout identity forces \(p\mid320\), contradicting \(p>5\).
